# Buyer Quirk Sheet: Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa (PRASA)

**Buyer:** Passenger Rail Agency of South Africa (PRASA)
**Kind:** State-Owned Entity (SOE) — national passenger rail operator
**Packs sampled:** 10 — ocds-9t57fa-165742, ocds-9t57fa-164172, ocds-9t57fa-164855, ocds-9t57fa-165777, ocds-9t57fa-165030, ocds-9t57fa-164088, ocds-9t57fa-165513, ocds-9t57fa-165416, ocds-9t57fa-165351, ocds-9t57fa-164227
**Date:** 2026-08

Note: ocds-9t57fa-165416 is a Bill of Quantities/pricing schedule annexure (numeric BOQ export) with no narrative conditions text; it was skimmed but contributed no citable claims below.

---

## Submission channel & rules

PRASA runs a **physical, sealed-envelope/box submission model** — no e-submission portal for bids. The National Treasury e-Tender Portal (www.etenders.gov.za) is used only to publish/download documents and post award results, not to receive bids.

- "Proposals must reach the PRASA before the closing hour on the date shown on SBD1 above and must be enclosed in a sealed envelope." (ocds-9t57fa-165742, ocds-9t57fa-164855, ocds-9t57fa-165030, ocds-9t57fa-165513, ocds-9t57fa-165351 — identical RFQ boilerplate)
- RFPs use a physical drop address: "Proposal Responses should be submitted to PRASA in a sealed envelope addressed as follows: The Secretariat / Tender Office" (ocds-9t57fa-164172, ocds-9t57fa-165777, ocds-9t57fa-164088)
- Bid boxes are named/numbered at regional offices: "BID RESPONSE DOCUMENTS MAY BE DEPOSITED IN THE BID BOX 6 SITUATED AT... PRASA REGIONAL OFFICE FOYER AREA" (ocds-9t57fa-165030)
- **Dual/triple-envelope packaging for RFPs**, separating technical from price: "All responses to the RFP should be submitted in two sealed envelopes/boxes; the first envelop/box shall have the technical, compliance and Specific goal response, the second envelop/box shall only have the financial response (Tender Form C and Price schedule)." (ocds-9t57fa-164088) — the panel-supplier RFPs (ocds-9t57fa-164172, ocds-9t57fa-165777) instead call for a single combined envelope/box ("8.1 All responses to the RFP should be submitted in a sealed envelopes/box; the envelop/box shall have the technical and compliance response").
- **Format redundancy required but not adjudicated by hierarchy** — original hard copy plus electronic copy on physical media, and PRASA states it will accept whichever format has the content (no explicit "hard copy governs" clause found): "Bidders must submit 1 original response and may submit copies and an electronic version which must be contained in a Memory Card/External hard drive etc clearly marked in the Respondents name. PRASA reserves the right to consider information provided in all formats irrespective the format i.e original/copy/electronic." (ocds-9t57fa-164088); reinforced generically as "Submit the tender as an original plus 1 copy and an electronic version which should be contained in Memory Cards clearly marked in the Bidders name" (ocds-9t57fa-164172, ocds-9t57fa-165777)
- Late/misdirected bids are a hard fail: "As a general rule, if a bid is late or delivered to the incorrect address, it will not be accepted for consideration." (ocds-9t57fa-164088)
- Compulsory bid-submission register/sign-in also required at drop-off for at least one RFP: "Bidders must complete a bid submission register and sign it" (ocds-9t57fa-165742)

## Municipal-arrears / rates clause

**Not observed in sampled packs.** No clause requiring bidders to be "not more than 90 days in arrears" on municipal rates/services was found in any of the 10 packs; no municipal-account-good-standing certificate is listed as a mandatory returnable. "Municipal" references in these packs relate only to localisation/geographic preference points (see Distinctive quirks below), e.g. "Business Address located within Ethekwini municipal boundary... Utility statement/municipal council letter" (ocds-9t57fa-165777) — this is a specific-goals scoring input, not a compliance/arrears gate.

## B-BBEE treatment

B-BBEE is used as **preference points only** under the standard PPPFA 80/20 system (never observed as a hard pre-qualification gate on its own) — B-BBEE certificates/affidavits are collected as returnable documents feeding the "Specific Goals" score, alongside separate localisation and ownership goals:

- "THE 80/20 PREFERENCE POINT SYSTEMS" applied consistently, e.g. "RFQ Proposal will be evaluated based on Preferential system & Price in accordance with the preference point system of 80/20 as per PRASA Preferential Policy" (ocds-9t57fa-165777); the SBD 6.1 form confirms the statutory threshold: "the 80/20 system for requirements with a Rand value of up to R50 000 000... and the 90/10 system for requirements with a Rand value above R50 000 000" (ocds-9t57fa-164227)
- Specific-goals scorecards typically split points across **B-BBEE level + 51% Black-owned + localisation**, e.g. "B-BBEE Level 1 5... 51% Black Owned 5... Localisation Within eThekwini Municipality boundary... 5" (ocds-9t57fa-165030); another pack scores "Entities with a B-BBEE contributor status of at least level 2 - B-BBEE Certificate/Affidavit 10; 51% Black Owned - CIPC Documents/B-BBEE Certificate/Affidavit 10; Total 20" (ocds-9t57fa-165030, second RFQ in the same pack)
- JV/consortium participation with B-BBEE entities is explicitly accommodated at submission stage: "Respondents who would wish to respond to this RFP as a Joint Venture [JV] or consortium with B-BBEE entities, should state their intention to do so in their RFP submission." (ocds-9t57fa-164172, ocds-9t57fa-164088, ocds-9t57fa-165777)
- Post-award, B-BBEE certificates must stay valid for the contract's life or PRASA can terminate: "The successful Respondent will be required to ensure the validity of all returnable documents, including but not limited to its Tax Clearance Certificate and valid B-BBEE Verification Certificate, for the duration of any contract... [failure entitles PRASA] to terminate such Agreement forthwith" (ocds-9t57fa-164172, ocds-9t57fa-165777, ocds-9t57fa-164088)

## Cure/condonation policy

No pack uses the words "condonation" or "cure period," but a de facto **two-tier fatal-vs-curable system** is visible and consistent:

- **Curable** — incomplete *returnable documents* trigger a resubmission window rather than instant disqualification: "Responsive bidder/s with incomplete returnable documents will be requested to resubmit completed documents within the timeframe provided by PRASA, failure which will result in automatic disqualification." (ocds-9t57fa-165030, ocds-9t57fa-164172, ocds-9t57fa-165777) — note the cure right attaches only to bidders already found "responsive"; the resubmission deadline is buyer-set and unspecified in days.
- **Fatal/non-curable** — mandatory Stage 1 compliance items and compulsory-briefing non-attendance cause immediate, automatic disqualification with no cure path: "Bidders must comply with the following requirements and failure to comply will lead to immediate disqualification... If you do not submit/meet the following mandatory documents/requirements, your bid will be automatically disqualified" (ocds-9t57fa-165742); "Bidders failing to attend the compulsory tender briefing session will be disqualified." (ocds-9t57fa-164227)
- Signature omissions are also fatal, not curable: "Failure to complete and sign the above confirmation will result in automatic disqualification." (ocds-9t57fa-165742)
- BOQ completeness is fatal in at least one RFQ: "Completion of all items in the bill of quantities (BOQ), failure which will result to automatic disqualification." (ocds-9t57fa-165030)

## Security/vetting requirements

- **Bidder-side security self-declaration ("Form F: Security Screening Form")** is a standard annexure in the KZN OHTE/electrical-material RFPs, requiring a sworn no-convictions declaration plus full banking and director details at submission: "I/We the under-signed... hereby declare that I/we do not have previous conviction/s or civil Judgment/s registered against my/our name/s... no criminal or civil proceeding pending..." with fields for Bank Name/Acc Number/Branch Code and Directors'/Trustees' ID numbers (ocds-9t57fa-164227). Security (guarding) providers must additionally attach "a letter of GOOD STANDING from PSIRA" (ocds-9t57fa-164227).
- **Not observed**: an integrity-pact document or explicit POPIA-consent clause aimed at all bidders generally.
- POPIA compliance appears as a service-specific requirement in the one pack that is itself an RFQ to hire a pre-employment screening/vetting contractor for PRASA's own new hires: "The service provider must be POPIA complaint 'certification' submitted with quote" and the scope covers SAQA/SAPS/Home Affairs/CIPC/ITC checks on PRASA's own promoted or externally appointed staff (ocds-9t57fa-165030) — this is a vetting *service being procured*, not a general bidder-vetting requirement PRASA imposes across all tenders.

## Financial demands

- **Financial capability is scored inside functionality**, not gated by a flat insurance/bank-letter threshold: bidders submit "two (2) recent year's annual financial statements prepared and signed by the registered professional and company director" and are scored 0–5 on an Operating Cash Flow Ratio (Cash Flows from Operations/Current Liabilities), with 0 points for no submission and 5 points for ratio ≥1 (ocds-9t57fa-164088).
- General financial-statement requirement echoed across RFPs: "Respondents are required to submit their latest financial statements prepared and signed off by a professional accountant" (ocds-9t57fa-164172, ocds-9t57fa-165777, ocds-9t57fa-164088).
- **Insurance is category-driven, not a fixed Rand figure**: some categories require none ("4.1.2 No insurance required... Service provider is responsible for the goods, until is successfully delivered in PRASAs warehouse" — stationery panel, ocds-9t57fa-165777) while works/plumbing categories require "Public liability insurance... Contractor related insurance" (ocds-9t57fa-164088) and electrical-material categories require "Insurance against Works and Goods" plus "Insurance against public liabilities (death or injury to any person, or loss of or damage to any property)" (ocds-9t57fa-164172). A generic clause also flags professional indemnity: "Bidders will be required to submit with their Bid for services professional indemnity insurance and works insurance" (ocds-9t57fa-164172, ocds-9t57fa-165777, ocds-9t57fa-164088). No specific insured amounts (Rand figures) were found in the sampled text.
- Standard cancellation-for-non-performance clause covers guarantees/bonds generically without prescribing amounts: "When a successful bidder has failed to provide the necessary security, bonds or guarantees within the time required to do so by PRASA" (ocds-9t57fa-164855, ocds-9t57fa-165030, ocds-9t57fa-165513, ocds-9t57fa-165351).
- **Not observed**: specific bank confirmation-letter or credit-rating requirements, or a stated minimum professional-indemnity/insurance Rand value.

## Functionality norms

Functionality (called "Technical/Functionality") is a hard, staged gate before price/specific-goals scoring, with thresholds varying by pack — 70% in some Western Cape/KZN RFPs, 80% in most others:

- "The minimum threshold for technical evaluation is [80%], any bidder who fails to meet the minimum requirement will be disqualified and not proceed with the evaluation of Price and Specific Goals." (ocds-9t57fa-165742)
- "The minimum threshold for the Technical/functionality criteria is (70%) and bidders who score below this minimum will not be considered for further evaluation" (ocds-9t57fa-164855)
- "The minimum threshold for technical evaluation is [70%]" (ocds-9t57fa-164088, plumbing RFP) vs "Threshold of 80%" (ocds-9t57fa-165777, 165513, 165351, stationery/other RFQs) — threshold appears set per-category rather than being a fixed house rule.
- Consistent 3-stage architecture: "Stage 1: Disqualifying Returnable documents; Stage 2: Technical/Functional Requirements (minimum threshold 80 points); Stage 3: Returnable Documents" then Price 80 / Specific Goals 20 (ocds-9t57fa-165777, and mirrored in ocds-9t57fa-164172, ocds-9t57fa-165513, ocds-9t57fa-165351).
- If nobody clears the bar, PRASA can scrap the process: "If all bidders score below the 80 points thresholds, PRASA reserves the right to cancel the bid and re-advertise or source using other procurement methods." (ocds-9t57fa-164172)

## Distinctive kill rules / quirks

- **Bidder-side sworn Security Screening Form with full banking/director disclosure** submitted with the bid itself (not just at award) — an unusual amount of financial/personal detail (bank account number, branch code, director ID numbers, criminal-record declaration) required as a standard bid annexure in KZN infrastructure-material RFPs (ocds-9t57fa-164227). Not seen in the RFQ-format packs.
- **Localisation preference points tied to municipal boundary**, stacked on top of B-BBEE: bidders score extra Specific Goals points for being physically located "Within eThekwini Municipality boundary according to the Municipal Demarcation Board," evidenced by "Municipal councillor letter or Municipal utility bill or Lease agreement" (ocds-9t57fa-165030) — a hyper-local geographic gate uncommon among generic national buyers.
- **Rural-residency preference tier**: extra points for individuals "living in the rural areas," evidenced by "Municipal/ESKOM bill or letter from Induna/chief confirming residential address not older than 3 months" (ocds-9t57fa-165513, ocds-9t57fa-165351) — traditional-authority (Induna/chief) letters as an accepted evidentiary document is distinctive.
- **Compulsory pre-tender briefing/site inspection with non-attendance = automatic disqualification**, applied broadly across both RFQ and RFP formats, and sometimes gating access to bid documents: "Arrangements can be made to make bids available before closing date provided that the prospective bidder has attended the compulsory briefing meeting... Bidders failing to attend the compulsory tender briefing session will be disqualified." (ocds-9t57fa-164227)
- **Complaints channel published directly on the tender document** rather than routed through a generic ombud: "Bidders are advised utilize this email address (Complaints@prasa.com) for lodging of complaints to PRASA in relation to this bid process." (ocds-9t57fa-165030, ocds-9t57fa-165513, ocds-9t57fa-165351, ocds-9t57fa-164855) — one pack uses a distinct address, "SCM.Complaints@prasa.co.za" (ocds-9t57fa-165742), showing address drift between regions/packs.
- **No-canvassing warning tied to disqualification** appears verbatim in every RFQ pack: "Respondent/s are warned that a response will be liable for disqualification should any attempt be made either directly or indirectly to canvass any SCM Officer(s) or PRASA employee in respect of this RFQ between the closing date and the date of the award of the business." (ocds-9t57fa-165742, ocds-9t57fa-164855, ocds-9t57fa-165030, ocds-9t57fa-165513, ocds-9t57fa-165351)
- **National Industrial Participation Programme (NIP/SBD5) obligation** appears for larger material-supply tenders, requiring the winning contractor to negotiate directly with the dti: "the contractor will submit a performance guarantee to the DTI; the contractor will submit a business concept for consideration and approval by the DTI" (ocds-9t57fa-164227) — an extra post-award workstream not typical of smaller-value SOE tenders.
- **"As and when required" panel/term contracts are the dominant vehicle**: nearly every sampled RFP appoints a panel of 3+ suppliers for 36-month as-and-when call-off arrangements rather than single-award fixed-scope contracts (ocds-9t57fa-164172, ocds-9t57fa-165777, ocds-9t57fa-164088, ocds-9t57fa-164227), meaning functionality/price scoring determines panel *ranking*, not a single winner.
